It handles daily central Party work, decides major state matters and emergencies, and receives reports from the State Council’s Party group. The Secretariat is a supporting body. This counting choice retains the Standing Committee alongside the general secretary’s personal authority.

Plenum and membership searches found no additional Standing Committee appointment, removal, death or interruption; changes to the wider Politburo were checked separately and do not change this unit.

office_chains.scope_notes: Include the vice-president of government as a subordinate head of government administration. Article 69 and decree 0237, Articles 2–3, assign government-wide coordination, coherent policy implementation, interministerial chairmanship and access to ministerial reports. Together these powers establish administrative leadership beyond a sector or advisory role. Presidential supremacy is also compatible with the included subordinate offices in Namibia, Mozambique and Tanzania, although their texts use more explicit headship language. The secretariat-general’s overlapping technical and arbitration duties do not make these powers exclusive, and exclusivity is not required. Decree 0314 expands Immongault’s personal arbitration and ordinary-management powers only from 29 June 2026. The narrower interpretation treats the earlier role as coordination under the president; inclusion rests on its combined government-wide responsibilities and reporting requirements.

office_chains.scope_notes: The Politburo is included as the standing collective authority directing national Party and state policy. A contemporary assessment of 2015–2017 practice identifies its national policy role and final authority over macroeconomic decisions. The 2021 Party statute gives it decisions on state organization, senior appointments, defence and foreign policy, and oversight of the General Secretary. The Central Committee retains higher policy, election and oversight powers. The nested Party leadership is counted once through the standing Politburo; the larger Central Committee is not a second collective sequence. The Secretariat assists implementation. Personal Party leadership and constitutional state offices are tracked separately.
office_chains.continuity_notes: The 2016 roster and the 2021 account of two departures and four entrants establish the opening eleven-member body and its successor. Phankham’s departure is bounded between his last positive membership description on 30 December 2022 and the official report calling him a former member on 20 November 2025; his premiership retirement is not automatically treated as his Party departure. The latter report names all twelve remaining members. The January 2026 election, Xaysomphone’s death on 8 August and Thongsavanh’s election during the 28 September–1 October plenum complete the intervening sequence. The revised 15 October roster, published again near cutoff, and dated November activity support continuation through 11 November under the elected term. The two bounded dates are retained explicitly; they do not overlap another composition change or alter event grouping.

The surviving effects of earlier orders do not extend the council’s own authority through the later study period.

office_chains.scope_notes: The assembly and its presidium are excluded from collective executive membership counting. The 2017 and 2023 assemblies have substantial binding constitutional and policy-approval powers. CRS describes the current Council’s powers as exceeding the president’s, and ODIHR calls it a supreme constitutional authority. This evidence is retained. The adopted classification treats its approval and supervisory functions as representative authority: other state organs implement its decisions within their own powers, while delegated presidential powers and succession belong to its chair personally. The presidium prepares meetings and proposals. The separate personal governing authority of Gurbanguly is included. This is a reasoned boundary between representative and executive headship, not a claim that the assembly is merely advisory.
office_chains.continuity_notes: The Council of Elders is transformed into the representative Halk Maslahaty in 2017, which first meets in 2018; a parliamentary upper chamber replaces it from 2021; the broad representative assembly returns in January 2023. These institutional changes are reviewed here. Their legislative and supervisory authority does not by itself meet the atlas’s executive-headship rule. The personal authority of Gurbanguly is retained in the separate National Leader chain.

office_chains.continuity_notes: Fourteen changes connect the nineteen-member opening roster to the nineteen-member Fourteenth Politburo at the cutoff. Medical leave, Secretariat assignments, state-office changes and sanctions against former members are distinguished from Politburo entry or exit.

The record treats the statutory transfer of functions as a substantive interim succession.

events.summary: Almazbek Baatyrbekov acquired statutory acting prime-ministerial powers on 9 October 2020 after Boronov was relieved of those duties. How this overlapped with Japarov’s accession remains unresolved.
events.caveats: Japarov’s assumption of governing authority is recorded within 6–12 October 2020. That interval may overlap Baatyrbekov’s statutory acting succession. The legal provision and deputy speaker’s account do not establish an uncontested transfer from Baatyrbekov to Japarov. The order and extent of the overlap remain unresolved, so these records do not form a settled three-person sequence.
events.date_basis: Boronov’s 9 October release from acting duties invoked Government Law Article 23(5), which vests those powers in the acting first vice-PM. The formal chronology identifies Baatyrbekov as that ex officio holder from 9 October, and the First Deputy Speaker expressly identified him as acting PM on 11 October. Retain 9 October as the statutory vesting date, without treating it as proof of exclusive practical control.

events.summary: Randrianirina assumed presidential authority during the military takeover on 14 October 2025.
events.caveats: The military announced a committee to govern and suspension of several institutions. The HCC’s 14 October decision nevertheless continued ordinary institutional powers while assigning the presidency to military authority embodied by Randrianirina. Its 18 November interpretation describes a five-officer structure tasked with leading the country, with Randrianirina as president and four high councillors assisting him. The court assigns the presidential functions and regulatory power to Randrianirina; the other four receive assistance roles and head-of-state benefits. On that allocation, the atlas records one personal presidential head and does not add a separate collective presidency. The 17 October oath confirms the effective 14 October transfer.
events.authority_status: military transitional government; prior president disputed legality
events.date_basis: effective takeover and court attribution of authority on 14 October

The acting-presidential date follows from that operative rule and appointment; his July ICC declaration corroborates subsequent exercise.

limits: Office and authority handovers are not regime changes or unique political episodes.
Collective composition changes use a separate unit and are not added to the handover total.
Country coverage status assesses completion under the stated definition, not a measured probability of complete discovery.
Country and regional totals vary with the number and kinds of executive offices tracked.
Calendar years 2016 and 2026 are partially observed; cross-year date ranges are not assigned to a guessed year.
Mechanism is a primary coding label; unclear governing-group changes are not interpreted as continuity.
Sensitivity scenarios alter specified inclusion rules only and do not bound all possible omissions.

categories.electoral_function_transfer: Temporary electoral transfer or resumption of presidential functions while the incumbent retains the mandate

categories.same_holder_return_after_legal_vacancy: Same holder resumes office after a documented legal interruption, including formal renewals following expiry or express termination.
